newsitem.title: USA: Allstate to sell property coverage in Calif.
newsitem.headline: Allstate to sell property coverage in Calif.

text.p: Allstate Corp's Allstate Insurance Co said on Monday that it soon will resume normal business operations in California, including the sale of property insurance.

The resumption follows passage of the California Earthquake Authority legislation, which creates a pool for providing earthquake insurance. It becomes operational when at least 70 percent of the state's residential property insurance market agrees to participate and the necessary commitments from reinsurers are obtained.
The Department of Insurance has said it expects the California Earthquake Authority to be selling policies by December 1.
Allstate said it intends to participate and its $150 million initial payment to the California Earthquake Authority will be included in the company's third-quarter results.

Allstate also said it would be obligated to pay additional assessments of about $750 million should the initial capitalization and retained earnings of the California Earthquake Authority be exhausted by claim payments.
